raw_case_text: A 62-year-old male took dexamethasone tablets (2.25 mg three times per day) and ornidazole tablets (0.5g two times per day) orally after tooth extraction. Ten days later, he developed fever (body temperature of 39 C) accompanied by chills, headache, bloating, tinnitus, and hearing loss. Treatment at the local hospital was not effective, and he was transferred to our hospital three days later. On admission, the patient's body temperature was 38.6 C, blood pressure was 134/74 mmHg, respiration was 16 beats/min, heart rate was 75 beats/min, and he was conscious. Relevant examinations were as follows: white blood cell count of 4.40x109/L, neutrophil percentage of 89.8%, lymphocyte count of 0.17x109/L, CD4+ lymphocyte count of 32/mm3, C-reactive protein level of 14.38 mg/L, creatinine level of 37.05 umol/L, pH of 7.399, procalcitonin level of 0.123 ng/mL, and 1,3-beta-d-glucan level of 253.73 pg/mL. Cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed multiple lesions in the brain. Enhanced MRI of the head showed multiple abnormal enhancement shadows in the brain: hematogenous disseminated lesions were possible. Chest computed tomography (CT) showed multiple ground-glass opacities in the anterior segment and lower lobe of the left lung. The patient's cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) had a white blood cell count of 1352x106/L, neutrophil percentage of 92%, glucose level of 0.59 mmol/L, and protein level of 1.48 g/L. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) of the patient's CSF reported 37,235 sequences from N. farcinica and 8 sequences from human cytomegalovirus. Blood NGS reported 61 sequences from Nocardia farcinica, 543 sequences from human cytomegalovirus, and 8 sequences from P. jirovecii. The patient's condition gradually deteriorated, and he developed confusion and respiratory failure, requiring an invasive ventilator to assist breathing. After a week of treatment with meropenem, compound sulfamethoxazole (SMZ), linezolid, and ganciclovir, the patient's symptoms improved slightly and he could breathe independently (Figure 1). On the 18th day, the patient's sputum culture was positive for A. fumigatus and lung CT showed new lesions. N. farcinica and P. jirovecii were not found in the sputum culture and we did not perform NGS again. The doctor administered voriconazole by intravenous drip (400 mg every 12 hours on the first day then 200 mg every 12 hours) to fight infection. The patient showed minimal response for about a week, with occasional hemoptysis, and the voriconazole trough concentration was 0.8 mg/L. We added oral omeprazole to the patient's regimen. On the 31st day, the patient's voriconazole trough concentration was 1.1 mg/L, and the blood no longer appeared in the sputum. CT showed that the lesions were absorbed better than before. The patient still had occasional headaches. On the 35th day, head MRI still revealed multiple infection lesions, similar to previous scans (Figure 2). We replaced meropenem with imipenem. On the 70th day, head MRI revealed a significantly reduced number of lesions. On the 78th day, the patient was transferred to a local hospital for continued treatment, and the treatment plan was changed to SMZ combined with linezolid, amoxicillin, and clavulanate potassium. The patient fully recovered after six months of treatment.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 62-year-old male presented with a 13-day history of high fever (up to 39 °C), chills, headache, abdominal bloating, tinnitus, and hearing loss that began 10 days after taking oral dexamethasone and ornidazole for a tooth extraction.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Following a dental extraction, the patient took oral dexamethasone (2.25 mg TID) and ornidazole (0.5 g BID). Ten days later, he developed high fever (39 °C), chills, headache, bloating, tinnitus, and hearing loss. After 3 days of ineffective treatment at a local hospital, he was transferred to our institution, where he subsequently developed confusion and acute respiratory failure requiring invasive mechanical ventilation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Recent tooth extraction treated for 10 days with oral dexamethasone (2.25 mg three times daily) and ornidazole (0.5 g twice daily).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for high fever (39 °C), chills, headache, tinnitus, hearing loss, abdominal bloating, and subsequent confusion, respiratory failure, and hemoptysis.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vital signs: Body temperature 38.6 °C, blood pressure 134/74 mmHg, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, heart rate 75 beats/min, and initially conscious before deteriorating into confusion and acute respiratory failure requiring endotracheal intubation.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission blood tests: WBC 4.40 x 10^9/L (89.8% neutrophils), severe lymphopenia with absolute lymphocyte count 0.17 x 10^9/L, C-reactive protein (CRP) 14.38 mg/L, serum creatinine 37.05 μmol/L, arterial pH 7.399, and procalcitonin 0.123 ng/mL. Lumbar puncture / cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis: Neutrophilic pleocytosis with WBC 1,352 x 10^6/L (92% neutrophils), hypoglycorrhachia with CSF glucose 0.59 mmol/L, and elevated CSF protein 1.48 g/L. Day 18 sputum culture: Positive for Aspergillus fumigatus.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission immunological and fungal biomarkers: Profound CD4+ T-cell depletion with CD4+ count of 32/mm3; elevated serum 1,3-beta-D-glucan at 253.73 pg/mL. Admission neuroimaging and chest CT: Cranial contrast-enhanced MRI demonstrated multiple ring/nodular enhancing parenchymal brain abscesses consistent with hematogenous dissemination; chest CT showed multiple ground-glass opacities in the left upper lobe anterior segment and left lower lobe (with new pulmonary lesions appearing on day 18). Paired CSF and peripheral blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS): CSF mNGS detected Nocardia farcinica (37,235 sequence reads) and human cytomegalovirus (8 reads); peripheral blood mNGS detected Nocardia farcinica (61 reads), human cytomegalovirus (543 reads), and Pneumocystis jirovecii (8 reads).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Disseminated Nocardia farcinica infection (purulent meningitis/multiple brain abscesses and bloodstream infection confirmed by 37,235 CSF mNGS reads and 61 blood mNGS reads) co-infected with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and cytomegalovirus (confirmed by blood mNGS [8 P. jirovecii and 543 CMV reads], serum 1,3-beta-D-glucan 253.73 pg/mL, and left lung ground-glass opacities) and secondary hospital-day-18 invasive pulmonary Aspergillus fumigatus infection, precipitated by post-dental dexamethasone therapy and severe CD4+ lymphopenia (32/mm3). Plan and clinical course: Managed with invasive mechanical ventilation, intravenous meropenem (later switched to imipenem on day 35), compound sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX), linezolid, and ganciclovir, allowing ventilator weaning within 1 week. When day 18 sputum culture grew A. fumigatus with new lung lesions and hemoptysis, intravenous voriconazole (400 mg q12h loading, 200 mg q12h maintenance) was added, and oral omeprazole was co-administered via CYP2C19 inhibition to boost subtherapeutic voriconazole troughs from 0.8 mg/L to 1.1 mg/L by day 31, resolving hemoptysis and lung lesions. Brain MRI lesions regressed by day 70; he was transferred on day 78 on oral TMP-SMX, linezolid, and amoxicillin-clavulanate and achieved complete recovery after 6 months of treatment.
